AIC = 111.8125 (rounded; exact = 111.8124599252796) for the logistic regression with BMI as the sole predictor of treatment response (efficacy PR).

Details: complete-case n = 80 (41 PR responders vs 39 PD/SD non-responders); k = 2 estimated parameters (intercept + BMI slope); maximum log-likelihood = -53.9062300; AIC = -2·logLik + 2·k = 111.8124599252796 (statsmodels LogitResults.aic agrees exactly with the manual computation).

Fitted model: logit(P(PR)) = -3.631934 + 0.167746·BMI (SE: intercept 2.1593, BMI 0.0979). Diagnostics: optimization converged, no perfect separation (fitted probabilities range 0.3515–0.6710), finite standard errors; AIC is therefore well-defined and trustworthy as a model-selection value. Note the BMI coefficient is not statistically significant at the 5% level (likelihood-ratio/z-based p ≈ 0.087), which does not invalidate the AIC.
